plugins.name: brand-capture
plugins.tagline: One-time brand setup. Scans a site and writes the brand files every other skill reads.
plugins.what: Builds BRAND.md once, when a client is set up, so no skill has to ask about the brand again. It scans the public website (about and story pages, products and prices, colors, fonts, blog style, social links, disclaimers) and reads any brand book you give it. It asks four short questions a website can't answer, then writes the brand files.
steps: It asks whether the brand has an existing store or website and a brand book, and which draft theme should hold the brand files.
It scans the website and reads the brand book if you provided one.
It asks four questions in one message: top competitors, inspiration brands, who approves things, and anything the brand must never say or claim.
It writes the files and asks at most four follow-up questions for anything the scan could not settle.
produces: BRAND.md (brand identity, the source of truth)
BRAND-VOICE.md (how the brand sounds)
design.md (palette, type, spacing, corners, components, imagery)
BRAND.html (a readable copy for the client)
BRAND-QUESTIONS.md (open follow-up questions)
guardrails: Scans public pages only.
Optional shared copy of the non-confidential files for the team.

plugins.name: competitor-research
plugins.tagline: Dated research on the competitors and inspiration brands named in BRAND.md.
plugins.what: Turns the competitors and inspiration brands the client named into COMPETITORS.md. For each one it compares where they operate against the client, what they sell and at what price, pricing model (flat, packages, memberships, subscriptions), offers and referral programs, how often they publish and who writes it, and how they position themselves. It ends with concrete openings for the client.
steps: It reads the competitor and inspiration lists from BRAND.md.
It researches each brand and compares it with the client.
It writes COMPETITORS.md next to BRAND.md and lists openings for the client.
produces: COMPETITORS.md (dated, re-run every few months)
guardrails: Never changes BRAND.md.

plugins.name: styles-builder
plugins.tagline: Turn a brand book or reference store into design tokens and apply them to the theme.
plugins.what: Creates or deepens design.md (typography, color schemes, spacing, corner radius, shadows, buttons, component states) and applies those tokens into the theme's settings_schema.json and settings_data.json. It also sets up what a new theme needs before pages get built: logo and favicon, motion, input fields, and variant pickers and swatches. Optionally it brands the starter section templates.
prompts: Set up the brand's colors and fonts in the theme
Get the theme ready to build on
steps: If BRAND.md or design.md are missing, it runs brand-capture first and waits for it to finish.
It builds the full token set from your brand book or a reference store.
It applies the tokens into the theme settings and sets up the starter essentials.
If you opted in at the start, it brands the starter section templates.
produces: design.md
Updated settings_schema.json and settings_data.json
Logo, favicon, motion, input and variant picker setup
guardrails: Starter section styling only happens if you opt in when it starts.

plugins.name: blog-generator
plugins.tagline: Research and write SEO and AEO blog posts, delivered as hidden Shopify drafts.
plugins.what: Writes blog posts meant to be found in Google and cited by AI answer engines. It asks intent, media, delivery, mode and topic once, reads BRAND.md and COMPETITORS.md instead of re-asking about the brand, researches what changes each time, and shows the outline for approval before writing.
prompts: Write a post for my store
Write a buying guide for X
Make a how-to article about X
I need a blog post for better SEO
steps: Answer the setup questions once: intent, media, delivery, mode, topic.
It researches the topic and shows the outline in chat.
You approve the outline.
It delivers a hidden Shopify draft, or paste-ready HTML, with SEO fields, images, schema and internal links.
produces: A hidden Shopify draft (via connector or browser), or paste-ready HTML
SEO fields, images, schema, internal links
requires: brand-capture (BRAND.md). competitor-research is optional but used when present.
guardrails: Posts land as hidden drafts for a human to review.
Guided mode or fully automated mode. Also runs from blog-autopilot.

plugins.name: blog-rewriter
plugins.tagline: Rewrite an existing article in the store's brand voice and post it as a hidden draft.
plugins.what: Takes a finished article written by someone else (a URL, Google Doc, .docx, .txt or .md file, or pasted text) and rewrites it in the store's voice. It is a voice transplant: facts and claims never change, only wording, tone, rhythm and terminology. Four depths are available: Match, Reword, Restructure and Reimagine.
prompts: Rewrite this doc for the blog
Put this article in our voice
Make this guest post on brand
Clean this up and post it as a draft
steps: Give it the article and choose a rewrite depth.
It rewrites in the voice from BRAND.md and the live blog, then fact-checks.
It posts a hidden draft with SEO fields and a preview link.
If Shopify is unavailable or not signed in, it returns paste-ready HTML and a fields sheet and says why.
produces: A hidden Shopify draft with SEO fields and a preview link
Fallback: paste-ready HTML and a fields sheet
guardrails: Never quietly changes a claim. Anything changed is flagged.
Posts are hidden drafts only.

plugins.name: blog-autopilot
plugins.tagline: Decides when a store should blog and what to cover, then hands off to the writer.
plugins.what: The editor-in-chief. It scans store events (new products, restocks, rising sellers), Search Console exports, review and helpdesk exports, competitor blog feeds, trends and an occasion calendar, scores the opportunities, and applies guardrails: dedupe, cannibalization, cooldowns and a weekly cap. It never writes the post itself.
prompts: What should we blog about this week?
Set up blogging on a schedule
Is anything worth a new post right now?
steps: It runs a weekly scan and scores opportunities.
By default it checks in with you and drafts only after you say yes.
It hands the brief to blog-generator, which writes a hidden draft.
Optional: turn on auto-draft.
produces: A ranked list of post opportunities
A brief handed to blog-generator
guardrails: Check-in first, draft only after approval, unless auto-draft is on.
Each brand keeps its own profile.

plugins.name: fact-check
plugins.tagline: Independent fact-check for blog and marketing copy, with guardrails for regulated claims.
plugins.what: Pulls out every factual claim, flags the risky ones (FDA and other regulatory status, medical and treatment claims, ingredient facts, pregnancy and safety statements, clinically proven, statistics), checks them against primary sources, and returns a claim-by-claim report with verdicts, citations and safer rewrites.
prompts: Check the FDA wording in this copy
steps: Give it pasted text, a file, a URL or a Shopify article.
It lists each claim and marks which are risky.
It verifies against authoritative sources.
You get verdicts, citations and safer wording.
produces: A claim-by-claim report with verdicts, citations and safer rewrites
requires: Nothing. Works on its own or after blog-generator.
guardrails: It flags and verifies. It never approves.
Regulated claims still need a qualified human or legal review.

plugins.name: seo-audit
plugins.tagline: Check a blog post after it goes live, then track real Search Console rankings.
plugins.what: Audits the live page with Google's own tools: structured data and Rich Results, PageSpeed Insights, title, meta, H1, leftover placeholders and indexing. About two and four weeks later it follows the post's real ranking numbers from Search Console.
prompts: How is the blog post doing in Google?
steps: Run it on publish day to check the live page.
Run it again around week 2 and week 4 for ranking numbers.
It can also run from a scheduled daily blog check.
produces: A live-page audit and ranking follow-ups at 2 and 4 weeks
guardrails: Read-only. It checks the post and changes nothing.

plugins.name: page-studio
plugins.tagline: Audit a page, then change it or build a new one on a draft theme.
plugins.what: Two skills that work together. page-audit is read-only: it checks a page against what its type should do and ranks the fixes. page-studio makes a named change (copy, image, link, section settings or order) or builds a new page, and can act on the recommendations an audit picked. It is built for the Site Editor, for marketing and ops people who aren't developers.

skills.name: page-audit
skills.tagline: Read-only gap analysis, ranked, with an owner for every fix.
prompts: What should we improve on the homepage?
Where does this page fall short?

skills.name: page-studio
skills.tagline: Make a named change or build a page on a draft theme.
prompts: Swap the image on the homepage hero
Make a landing page for X
Recreate this page from the live site
Swap the image on the homepage hero
Make a landing page for X
steps: Each skill first checks what it needs (a browser, the Shopify CLI, your brand files) and, if anything is missing, walks you through setting it up in plain steps.
Start with page-audit. Say what the page is for: book, sell, promote, build trust, inform or fix.
It checks the rendered page at desktop and mobile against a playbook for its type, and names who owns each fix (this theme, store admin, store settings, a third-party app, or an off-site page).
It writes a ranked report and a living PAGE-AUDIT.md.
Ask page-studio to apply the recommendations you pick, or name any change or new page directly.
produces: A client-ready audit report and PAGE-AUDIT.md
Changes or new pages on a draft theme
requires: brand-capture (BRAND.md, BRAND-VOICE.md, design.md) for new or rewritten words.

To change pages: Node.js, the Shopify CLI signed in to your store with theme access, a browser Claude can use, and a folder on your computer for the theme copy. page-audit needs only a browser and the page address.
No need to set these up in advance: each skill checks them first and walks you through anything missing, step by step.
guardrails: page-audit never edits a theme or store.
Changes go only to a draft theme (asked for or created). The live theme is never edited.

plugins.name: accessibility-audit
plugins.tagline: Lighthouse accessibility scoring for a Shopify theme, with additive fixes and re-scoring.
plugins.what: Scores a page with the Lighthouse CLI, classifies every failing audit, proposes minimal fixes, and after your approval applies them and re-scores until the page reaches 1.00. Fixes are additive only: aria attributes, roles, hidden labels, blank-value guards and a minimum contrast nudge. It never changes layout, styling or copy.
prompts: Run Lighthouse on the product page
steps: It checks what it needs (Node.js, the Shopify CLI, Chrome, Lighthouse) and walks you through setting up anything missing.
Pick the draft theme to work on. It asks once and remembers, or makes a draft copy. The live theme is never edited.
It scores the page and classifies each failing audit.
You approve the proposed fixes.
It applies them and re-scores until the page hits 1.00.
produces: A scored report and approved accessibility fixes
requires: Node.js, the Shopify CLI signed in to your store with theme access, Google Chrome, Lighthouse (downloads itself), a browser Claude can use, and a folder on your computer for the theme copy.
No need to set these up in advance: it checks them first and walks you through anything missing, step by step.
guardrails: Never edits the live theme: it works on a draft theme, asked for or created.
Roughly 15 to 40 minutes per page template. This is an estimate.

plugins.name: analytics
plugins.tagline: Audit tagging, get tracking working, clean up tags and keep it from breaking.
plugins.what: Four skills sharing one ANALYTICS.md per client site. Analytics is only useful if the numbers can be trusted, and most breakages are silent: a duplicated tag, a renamed button, a consent banner that never reports the visitor's choice. Shopify-first, also WordPress and custom sites.

skills.name: analytics-audit
skills.tagline: Tagging audit and full audit across privacy states. Changes nothing.
prompts: Is our analytics set up correctly?

skills.name: analytics-setup
skills.tagline: From the client's issue list to approved, verified fixes.

skills.name: analytics-cleanup
skills.tagline: Quick cleanup of dead tags, or zero-based deep tag cleanup.
prompts: Our site is slow because of tags

skills.name: analytics-guardrails
skills.tagline: Dependency register, change checks and drift watch.
prompts: Check analytics impact before this theme change

steps: Audit first: it inventories what is installed, what it sends and what should change, with evidence.
Setup runs the full path: issue list, tracking plan, audit, prioritised actions for approval, one fix at a time with a rollback ready, then re-test every core event.
Cleanup removes dead weight, then makes every remaining tag earn its place.
Guardrails checks every later site change against a register of what tracking depends on.
produces: ANALYTICS.md (tracking plan, stack inventory, consent setup, dependency register, findings, changelog)
requires: Python 3 for the scripts. The privacy matrix needs Node and Playwright. The cost benchmark needs Node and Chrome. GA4 checks can use Google's Analytics MCP server.
guardrails: Audit changes nothing.
Setup never skips the approval or the test.

plugins.name: cro-audit
plugins.tagline: Find what is costing conversions, say how sure we are, and plan what to fix and test.
plugins.what: A quick first-pass audit or the full research suite CRO agencies run, with no integrations required. It reviews the live page (technical, speed, mobile, heuristics, competitors), reads the store's Shopify Analytics read-only through the Shopify CLI (or numbers you supply), checks the data can be trusted (tracking breaks, orders by channel, bots), then analyses it by segment, reviews heatmaps and recordings you bring, mines reviews and support text, writes survey questions and user-test scripts and analyses the results. Every finding is labelled by the kind of evidence behind it and how confident we are. It then sorts issues into just do it, instrument, investigate, test or hypothesize, scores them, and plans experiments with a hypothesis, metrics, sample size and duration. It also checks A/B test results, including whether the traffic split was valid.
prompts: Run a CRO audit on the homepage
Run the full CRO research suite
Here are our funnel numbers, where is the leak?
Plan an A/B test for the booking button
How many visitors do we need for this test?
steps: Choose a quick audit (about an hour, needs nothing from you) or the full audit.
It reviews the live page at desktop and phone width and measures speed.

If the Shopify CLI is authorised for the store it reads the analytics itself, read-only; otherwise bring funnel numbers. Also bring heatmaps or recordings, reviews or support text, past test results if you have them.
It prepares the survey questions and user-test script if you want them, and analyses the answers when they come back.
It writes CRO-AUDIT.md: ranked findings with evidence and confidence, quick wins, an experiment roadmap and open questions.
produces: CRO-AUDIT.md (ranked findings with evidence and confidence, buckets, scores, experiment plans, open questions)
Survey questions and a user-test script, on request
requires: Nothing for a quick audit. For analytics: the Shopify CLI authorised for the store with read_reports and read_orders (you grant it yourself), or exported numbers. Uses REVIEW-MINING.md, COMPETITORS.md and BRAND.md if they exist.
guardrails: Strictly read-only: never changes store settings, setup, themes, content or apps, even with access that would allow it, and never submits forms or answers the cookie banner.
No invented benchmarks or lift predictions.
Small samples are flagged as directional.
It prepares surveys and tests but does not run them; you collect that data.
